content:
maria: Heads-up — found a tiny repro for a rollup/CJS interop bug that breaks the JS SDK's auth/retry wiring when apps consume our ESM bundle via require().

maria: Repro steps (super small):
```json
// package.json
{
  "name": "rollup-consumer-repro",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "type": "commonjs",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "rollup src/index.js --file dist/bundle.js --format cjs -p @rollup/plugin-commonjs -p @rollup/plugin-node-resolve"
  }
}
```

maria: src/index.js (consumer):
```js
const { RedwoodClient } = require('../node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/sdk.js');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
// hits: client.auth.getToken(...).retry(...) --> fails because auth is undefined
```

maria: After build: dist/bundle.js ends up with our SDK wrapped as { default: [Function: RedwoodClient] } and require() returns an object with .default. Our consumer code expects named export which sometimes gets lost by rollup/commonjs interop and then auth wrapper (attached at build-time) isn't present. Error seen at runtime:
```
TypeError: client.auth is not a function
    at Object.<anonymous> (app.js:12:23)
```

jon: Oof. Is this the same as default-vs-named weirdness? Could be consumer using require() but SDK published only as ESM default export.

kevin: Likely. Rollup commonjs plugin sometimes turns ESM default into module.exports.default. If our SDK attaches helpers by mutating the exported function in ESM build (e.g., export default with side-effects), the CJS consumer won't surface those side-effects unless they call .default.

maria: Minimal reproduction repo attached (private gist). Tried with rollup v3 + @rollup/plugin-commonjs and node 18. Repro steps: npm i, npm run build, node dist/bundle.js -> throw.

kevin: Quick workarounds for consumers:
- require('...').default || require('...') when loading the SDK
- enable compiler flags: tsconfig "esModuleInterop": true / "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true for TS consumers
- for rollup: use output.exports = 'auto' and add commonjs plugin config to transform default properly.

maria: We should also consider publishing a small CJS-compatible entry (main) that re-exports the ESM default in top-level shape so require() always gets the same runtime shape.

jon: Agreed. Also noticed this reproduces differently in edge SSR (Cloudflare/Node-Edge) because their bundlers do extra treeshake + rename. The auth/retry wrapper is attached lazily and end up tree-shaken in some builds.

maria: Example patch I tried in consumer to make it robust:
```js
const maybe = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const SDK = maybe && (maybe.default || maybe);
const client = new SDK.RedwoodClient ? new SDK.RedwoodClient(...) : new SDK(...);
```
Not pretty.

kevin: For SDK side we can do two small things that are low risk:
1) Publish a CJS shim file at `dist/index.cjs.js` that consumes the ESM build and sets module.exports = require('./esm.js').default || require('./esm.js') so older require() callers get the right object.
2) Add a unit test that bundles our published package with rollup (commonjs plugin) + a tiny consumer to assert runtime shape (client.auth exists and client.auth.retry is a function).

dev-bot: Created issue #2874: "cjs interop: ensure auth/retry preserved when consumed via require()" (assigned to eng-devex).

sara: I reproduced locally using rollup + node 18. Patch 1 works for me (simple CJS shim). I'll add the rollup-bundling regression test to CI and add a note in the release notes about the workaround for consumers.

jon: Can we also add a blurb in the SDK docs under "Node bundlers / CommonJS" with copy like:
- Prefer native ESM (import) when possible
- If you must use require(), use `const SDK = require('@redwood-inference/sdk').default || require('@redwood-inference/sdk')`
- For TypeScript, set esModuleInterop=true

maria: That should reduce onboarding friction. Also we should call out known edge/runtime bundlers (Vite SSR, Cloudflare Pages, Rollup CJS outputs) where we've seen this.

sara: I'll open a PR with the shim + CI test and link the issue. Leaving a note: this produced subtle auth/retry regressions in a couple of customer sample apps, so worth backporting to the last minor if possible.

jon: Thanks, folks. Short-term consumer workaround is documented, long-term fix is CJS shim + tests.

maria: TL;DR: rollup CJS interop can move our default export under .default, which breaks clients using require() and leads to missing auth/retry helpers. Patch: publish a CJS shim + add rollup-bundle test + doc note.

kevin: Also add an integration test that runs in a simulated edge bundler environment (vite-ssr build) — we saw different tree-shake behavior there.

maria: Agreed. I'll queue follow-ups in the issue. Thanks! :thumbsup:
